transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. Um, I hope I'm in the right place, but... I guess what finally pushed me to make this appointment is that I've been having a little bit of trouble at work. 

I'm an auditor, and I keep starting these follow-up items after my audits, or sometimes after mentorship events we host. And I have every intention of finishing them, I really do! I always try my best to do a good job. But then... well, I'll find out days later that the final email, or a review note, or some form just never actually got done. 

It's honestly a bit embarrassing to admit, because I know I should just finish them, but it just keeps happening. Is that the kind of thing you help people with? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Outside of these work tasks, do you find yourself forgetting things or having trouble staying focused in other areas of your life?

Um, yes, I suppose it does bleed over a little bit into other things. But I think it's mostly just normal busyness, you know? Like, I'll absolutely mean to do something, and I really try to stay on top of things, but sometimes little things just slip my mind. 

For example, I might forget to call a junior staff member back when I said I would, or... well, sometimes I'll miss paying a bill just before the late fee hits, even though I had the money and fully intended to do it. Or I'll agree to go to a mentorship event and then realize later I never actually put it on my calendar. 

I know it sounds a little disorganized, and I always feel terrible when it happens. I really don't want people to think I don't care, because I do! Does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Looking back, would you say you had similar issues with forgetfulness or staying on task when you were a child, say before age 12?

Um, well... I guess if I really think back to when I was little, maybe there were a few things. But I was a good student! I really was. My teachers always said I was bright, which was so nice of them. 

But, um... well, I suppose my report cards did sometimes mention that I would lose assignments, or maybe rush through things and miss a few small details. And I guess I might have talked out of turn once in a while, or needed a little nudge to finish my work. It wasn't because I was trying to be difficult, I promise! I just got so excited about things, you know? 

Actually, my mom still teases me about it sometimes. She jokes that I could ace a test without any problem, but then completely forget to turn in the big project that was sitting right there in my backpack. It sounds a little silly when I say it out loud... I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a bad kid? I really did try my best to be good. Is that the kind of childhood stuff you're looking for?
Do you also find yourself struggling with forgetfulness or staying on task during social events, hobbies, or other activities outside of work and home responsibilities?

Um, well... I guess I do sometimes have a little trouble staying totally focused, even when it's something I'm really interested in. But I think everyone gets a little distracted sometimes, right? 

Like, if I'm in a really long client meeting, or maybe taking one of those new AI-tool training courses for work... I'll start out so engaged, and I really do want to learn everything they're saying! But then, after a while, I guess my mind just sort of... slips away for a second. And then I'll suddenly realize I haven't actually heard the last few minutes of what was said, even though I've been sitting there looking right at the screen the whole time. 

I always feel so guilty when that happens, because I really respect the people presenting, and I don't want them to think I'm ignoring them. I always try to catch up right away! Is that... is that normal? I hope it doesn't make me sound rude.
Do you ever find yourself feeling restless, fidgety, or as if you can't sit still for very long, especially in situations where you're expected to stay calm and focused?

Um, well, I guess... maybe a little bit? I mean, I don't want to sound like I'm bouncing off the walls or anything, because I really do try to be professional. But, um... yeah, sitting perfectly still for a long time can be just a tiny bit tricky for me. 

Like, when I'm in those long accounting meetings, I might, you know, tap my foot under the table a little. Or sometimes I catch myself clicking my pen. I don't even realize I'm doing it! Or I'll just sort of... shift around in my chair a bit to get comfortable. Actually, my colleague joked the other day that she can hear my leg going under the desk. 

I was so embarrassed! I really try to keep it hidden because I know it can be distracting to other people, and the last thing I want is to bother anyone. It's just a little extra energy, I think. Does that make sense? I hope that doesn't make me sound like a disruption in the office.
Do you find that these difficulties with focus or restlessness also happen in other settings, like when you're at home relaxing, spending time with friends, or doing something you enjoy?

Um, well... I suppose it's not just at work, if I'm being completely honest. I mean, I really do try to relax when I'm at home, I promise! But, um, even when I'm doing something that's supposed to be calming, like trying to read a book on the couch, or... or even just waiting quietly before my salsa class starts, I find it a little hard to just... be still. 

I guess pure quiet just makes me feel a tiny bit antsy? So I might start humming a little tune without meaning to, or I'll pick up my phone to check something real quick, or I'll just start chatting with whoever is nearby. It's not that I don't enjoy the downtime! I just... I guess I just like to keep things a little lively. I really hope that doesn't make me sound annoying to be around. Do you think it's okay to be a little like that when you're just trying to unwind?
When you were a child, did you often have trouble sitting still or staying focused on tasks, even when you wanted to?

Um, well... I guess if I think back to when I was little, maybe there were a few signs? I mean, I really don't want to sound like I was a bad kid or anything! I always tried my best to be good and do what the teachers asked. 

But, um, I suppose even back in elementary school, my teachers would write on my report cards that I was bright—which was nice of them to say!—but that I sometimes... well, that I'd lose assignments or rush past some of the smaller details. And I guess I had a bit of a habit of talking out of turn sometimes, or needing a few extra reminders to finish my work. 

My mom actually still jokes about it sometimes. She says I could completely ace a test, but then totally forget to turn in the big project that was sitting right there in my backpack the whole time. I always felt so terrible when that happened! I really didn't mean to be careless, I just... things would slip my mind, I guess. Is that... do you think that's normal for kids? I hope it doesn't make me sound like I was a troublemaker.

Can you tell me if these experiences with focus and restlessness have been happening pretty consistently throughout your life, or if they’ve gotten worse at certain times, like during periods of stress or as you’ve gotten older?

Um, well... I guess they've always been there a little bit, like I said about when I was a kid. But I've always managed to get by, you know? I really pride myself on being a hard worker. 

But, um... if I'm being completely honest, things have gotten just a tiny bit more challenging lately. Not that I can't handle it! I'm really trying. It's just... about, I don't know, maybe a year and ten months ago, I won this firm-wide award, which was so wonderful and I was so grateful. And then I got a promotion right after that. 

Which is great! It's a really good thing. But the workload and all the new responsibilities... it's just been a little harder to juggle everything perfectly. I feel like the restless feeling and the trouble focusing have just been a bit more noticeable since then. I'm really trying my best to stay on top of it all, I promise. I just don't want anyone at work to think I'm not capable of doing the job, you know? Do you think it's normal for things to get a little harder when you get a big promotion like that?
